title: The 10 Best Cordless Shop Vacuums
subtitle: Battery-powered wet/dry shop vacs ranked from live Amazon data, from 2-gallon jobsite vacs to a 9-gallon garage vac.
intro: A cordless shop vac handles spills, car interiors, and jobsite dust without hunting for an outlet. Most best-sellers are 2 to 2.6-gallon vacs sold as bare tools for an existing battery platform; a few come as kits with batteries. We ranked 10 on rating, review volume, and features (a HEPA-rated filter, a blower function, a brushless motor, and whether a battery is included).
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.name: Rueqior Cordless Vacuum Compatible with DeWalt 20V Battery Handheld Vacuum
avoid.flag: A 0.7-liter handheld sold as a shop vacuum
avoid.verdict: It turns up in shop vac searches and calls itself a shop vacuum in its bullets, but it's a handheld car vac with a 0.7-liter bin, rated for indoor use on carpet and upholstery.
reasons: The capacity is 0.7 liters, under a fifth of a gallon. Every vac on this list holds at least 2 gallons.
The listing rates it for indoor use on carpet, upholstery and cars and never claims wet pickup, so it can't do the spill and jobsite cleanup a shop vac is for.
It's a third-party body for DEWALT 20V batteries, so DEWALT doesn't warrant it. DEWALT's own bare 20V vacs are on this list.

buyers_guide.q: Do cordless shop vacs have enough suction?
buyers_guide.a: For spills, car interiors, and jobsite dust, yes. Compact cordless vacs run roughly 35 to 57 CFM; plug-in shop vacs of similar size quote more. If you need to pull water out of a flooded basement, the 9-gallon EGO (110 CFM, 100 in. of water lift) is the only cordless pick here that's in that range.

buyers_guide.q: Should I buy a bare tool or a kit?
buyers_guide.a: If you already own DEWALT, Milwaukee, CRAFTSMAN, Makita, or EGO batteries, buy the bare vac on the same platform and save the battery cost. If you own none, a kit like the Seesii or WORX costs less than buying a name-brand bare vac plus a battery and charger.

buyers_guide.q: How long does a battery last in a shop vac?
buyers_guide.a: Vacs drain batteries fast. Listings on this page quote 20 to 30 minutes on a compact vac at full power, up to 80 minutes on low with two 4.0Ah batteries on the JESIMAIK, and up to 60 minutes in ECO mode on the EGO with two 6.0Ah packs. Plan on a spare battery for anything bigger than a car.

buyers_guide.q: What do CFM, water lift, and kPa mean?
buyers_guide.a: CFM is airflow, which moves light debris like sawdust. Water lift (in inches) and kPa both measure sealed suction, which lifts heavy debris and water. Brands publish different ones, so compare like with like: the Milwaukee M18 FUEL lists 50 CFM and 47 in. of lift; the JESIMAIK lists 18.5 kPa.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need a HEPA filter?
buyers_guide.a: For drywall, concrete, and sanding dust, yes; a regular filter lets fine dust blow back out the exhaust. Most vacs here ship with a HEPA-rated filter. The EGO and WORX use cartridge filters that aren't listed as HEPA.

buyers_guide.q: Can a cordless vac double as a dust extractor for my sander?
buyers_guide.a: None of the vacs here is sold as a dedicated dust extractor. They can connect to a tool's dust port with an adapter, but the compact tanks fill quickly.
